degree / Foundations of legal knowledge

The qualifying law degree must be compliant with the Quality Assurance Agency (QAA) subject benchmark statement for law and cover the following seven foundations of legal knowledge, which are:

Criminal Law

Equity and Trusts

Law of the European Union

Obligations 1 (Contract Law)

Obligations 2 (Tort Law)

Property/Land Law

Public Law (Constitutional Law, Administrative Law & Human Rights Law)

Degree stage

We welcome applications from people who graduated some time ago as well as those newly graduating.

Overseas degrees

We accept applications from candidates with overseas degrees. You must supply evidence that your degree is equivalent to the minimum requirement of a 2:2 honours in an UK undergraduate degree.

The responsibility (including any costs) of providing appropriate documentation is on the individual. The UK National Information Centre provides information about the comparability of different international qualifications.

We would normally ask for evidence when candidates are completing the online application form and situational judgement test.

Qualified lawyers / Overseas lawyers

The legal trainee scheme is for those who have not yet qualified as a lawyer. If you are qualified as a solicitor or barrister in England and Wales or have qualified as a lawyer in another jurisdiction, you will not be eligible to apply for the Legal Trainee Scheme.

If you are qualified to practise law in another jurisdiction, you may be able to re-qualify to practise in England and Wales through an alternative route. We recommend that you contact the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) and the Bar Standards Board (BSB) for further information.

Security Clearance

Some departments require their trainees to obtain higher-level security clearance prior to starting their training.

For applicants interested in roles within GLD, you will ideally be able to obtain Security Check (SC) clearance. Or, at minimum, you will need to obtain Counter Terrorist Check (CTC) clearance prior to starting the role.

For applicants interested in roles in HMRC and CMA, trainees may have the opportunity to obtain higher security clearance (for example, SC clearance), but you will only be required to obtain Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance prior to starting the role.

For applicants interested in roles in NCA, the NCA will conduct enhanced pre-employment checks, in addition to the minimum Security Check (SC) requirement, to determine suitability to work for an organisation combating serious and organised crime. All NCA officers must hold Enhanced Security Check (eSC) clearance upon entry as a minimum. Failure to achieve Enhanced SC clearance will result in the job offer being withdrawn. Individuals will be required to undertake and pass a substance misuse test as part of the pre-employment checks.

There are residency requirements for higher levels of clearance. Further information about clearance levels and requirements is available on GOV.UK.

What we look for

Factors such as the school you attended, A levels and GCSEs results, your university and degree subject do not form part of our decision-making process.

The type of skills and behaviours we are looking for and how we test them are below.

Person Specification

MS Word Document, 18.3 KB

Application & Assessment Centre stages

There are five parts to the recruitment and selection process:

An online application form and a situational judgement test

A verbal reasoning test

A critical reasoning test

A video interview

A half-day assessment centre

In the eventuality that there are a high number of high scoring candidates at the video interview and assessment centre stage, individuals may have their applications placed on hold where they have met the required standard. Should video interview and assessment centre spaces become available, candidates may be invited to participate.

Please note that there is no guarantee that being placed on hold means you will progress to video interview or assessment centre stage.

Offers will be made according to each location in merit order.

Situational judgement test (SJT)

The SJT assesses your judgement in dealing with the types of situations you may encounter as a legal trainee. If you pass the eligibility criteria in the application form, you will then receive an email inviting you to complete the SJT.

You will be given 16 hypothetical situations and a list of possible reactions to each situation. You will be asked to indicate which reaction you think would be the most effective response and least effective response to the situation.

The SJT is conducted online. The test is not timed but should take between 25 to 30 minutes to complete.

Example of SJT question

MS Word Document, 38.5 KB

This file may not be suitable for users of assistive technology.

Request an accessible format

If you use assistive technology (such as a screen reader) and need a version of this document in a more accessible format, please email govtrainees@tmpw.co.uk. Please tell us what format you need. It will help us if you say what assistive technology you use.

A free practice test can be found on the AssessmentDay website.

If you obtain the pass mark for the SJT, we will invite you to complete the Verbal Reasoning Test.

Verbal reasoning test (VRT)

Our legal trainees need to be able to analyse and interpret complex information. The VRT provides you with the opportunity to demonstrate your ability in this important area.

The VRT is conducted online and is timed. You will be given 24 minutes to complete the test.

A free practice test can be found on the AssessmentDay website.

If you obtain the pass mark for the VRT, we will invite you to complete the Critical Reasoning Test.

Critical reasoning test (CRT)

The CRT assesses your ability to logically analyse assumptions, arguments, deductions, inferences and interpret information.

passages.quote:
sability

We believe that all eligible people must have equality of opportunity for employment and advancement on the basis of their suitability for the work.

The Equality Act 2010 requires us to provide reasonable adjustments for disabled people.

This is defined by the Act as those who have a physical or mental impairment. For example a substantial and long-term adverse effect on that person’s ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities.

We will not make assumptions about whether a disabled person requires any adjustments or what those adjustments should be.

We will discuss and agree with the individual in question the reasonable adjustments required.

If you are a disabled person, as defined by the Equality Act 2010, and wish to request reasonable adjustments for any stage of the recruitment process, you must notify the Recruitment Team in your application form. This must be submitted by the stated deadline. Examples include additional time for the timed online tests and adjustments at the assessment centre.

If you require a reasonable adjustment to complete your application form and/or situational judgement test you will need to contact the Recruitment Team as soon as possible.

If you would find it helpful to discuss your requirements, please contact the Recruitment Team.

Any information provided in support of your request will be treated confidentially and withheld from those involved in selection decisions.

Monitoring

We will record and monitor the reasonable adjustments that have been requested and made. This will help us identify whether there are any wider steps that we can take to support those applying to us with a disability.

Disability Confident scheme

Departments recruiting under the legal trainee scheme have signed up to the Disability Confident scheme.

If you consider yourself to have a disability as defined by the Equality Act 2010, you can apply under the terms of the scheme.

To be invited to attend the assessment centre, you will need to:

Meet all aspects of the eligibility criteria

Meet the standard in each of the 3 online tests to be invited to complete a video interview

Be amongst the highest scoring candidates at the video interview stage to be invited to the final assessment centre stage.

Complaints procedure

The legal trainee scheme is underpinned by the principle of selection for appointment on merit on the basis of fair and open competition. This is outlined in the Civil Service Commission’s Recruitment Principles.

You have the right to complain if you feel there has been a breach of the Civil Service Recruitment Principles. If you feel that your application has not been treated in accordance with these Principles and wish to make a complaint, please contact Recruitment Feedback in the first instance. Please title your email as ‘Legal Trainee Scheme - Recruitment Complaint’.

Complaints must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the incident or the decision which has caused the complaint. To fully engage with the issues raised, you are required to submit evidence of your complaint.

Civil Service Code

As civil servants, legal trainees will be appointed on merit on the basis of fair and open competition.

Legal trainees will be expected to carry out their role with dedication and a commitment to the Civil Service and its core values: integrity, honesty, objectivity and impartiality:

‘integrity’ is putting the obligations of public service above your own personal interests

‘honesty’ is being truthful and open

‘objectivity’ is basing your advice and decisions on rigorous analysis of the evidence

‘impartiality’ is acting solely according to the merits of the case and serving equally well governments of different political persuasions

The core values are set out in the Civil Service Code.

Professional bodies’ requirements

If you are successful in obtaining a trainee solicitor or pupil barrister position, please ensure that you understand the requirements placed on you by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) or the Bar Standards Board (BSB)

For example, trainee solicitors (looking to qualify through the LPC route or SQE route) will need to meet the SRA’s character and suitability requirements.
